newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Firm wheat prices to sideline Philippine buyers.
newsitem.headline: Firm wheat prices to sideline Philippine buyers.

text.p: Rising U.S. wheat prices will cause Philippine flour millers to wait on the sidelines next week before making any buys, traders said on Friday.

"Wheat prices moved up last week and this is not a good omen to millers who are generally not interested to buy wheat at a higher price. On top of that, most of the local millers are fully stocked," a trader said.
Spring wheat prices in Minneapolis, where the Philippines buys most of its wheat, closed slightly higher on Thursday. December was up U.S. 1/4 cent to $4.20-1/4 a bushel.
Philippine millers did not buy any wheat this week. They were hoping to make some purchases due to bumper crops around the world, dealers said.

"We expected U.S. wheat prices to drop due to competition from Australia, Argentina and Canada. But U.S. stocks were tight since they exported so much last week. And if the frost situation does not change, we are looking at higher prices of wheat," one trader said.
Millers said they will wait for a U.S. report by the end of the month on the wheat supply and demand scenario.
A cancer scare over the use of potassium bromate which caused a 20 percent drop in bread sales adversely affected flour sales, the millers added.
The retail price of hard flour and soft flour was steady at 290 pesos and 260 pesos a kg, respectively, the Trade and Industry Department said.
The state-run National Food Authority said the retail price of white corn was unchanged at 10.67 pesos per kg while the price of yellow corn went up to 10.84 pesos per kg from 10.81 pesos last week.
